subject: chemistry
question_text: Give the ratio of RMS, average and most probable speeds of gas molecules.

verification.note: Chapter 4 (States of Matter) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.62-66), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The book prints NO Long Answer section for this chapter, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. ROUNDING: the book prints the ratio as 1 : 0.9213 : 0.8166. The exact third value is √(2/3) = 0.81650, which rounds to 0.8165. The card prints 0.8165 and records the book's 0.8166 here.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The three speeds
steps.why: All three speeds share the factor √(RT/M), so the ratio is fixed by the numbers under the roots alone — 3, 8/π and 2 — and is the same for every gas at every temperature.
common_mistakes: Mixing up which number goes with which speed: 3 with rms, 8/π with average, 2 with most probable.
Treating the ratio as temperature-dependent. The RT/M part cancels.
steps.memory_tip: Under the roots: 3, then 8 over π (about 2.5), then 2 — decreasing order, same as the speeds.
steps.margin_note: The three formulas justify the decimal ratio; either form earns the mark.

steps.label: The ratio
steps.why: Dividing each root by √3 gives 1, 0.9213 and 0.8165. Writing the ratio with rms scaled to 1 makes the other two speeds direct multipliers, which is exactly how numericals use them.
common_mistakes: Reversing the order — the most probable speed is the SMALLEST of the three.
Quoting 0.9213 against the most probable speed instead of the average.
steps.memory_tip: 1, then 0.92, then 0.82 — each about 8 to 10 percent below the one before.
steps.margin_note: Some books print 0.8166; the exact rounding of √(2/3) is 0.8165. Either is accepted.

insider_note: This ratio is also the working tool of the CO₂ speeds numerical — examiners reward students who know 0.9213 and 0.8165 as multipliers of the RMS speed.
